7. **Travel on the map, and news travels.** Distant provinces, and who holds them, show their last known state with its date; news travels with people ("Hidden by default"; question 6 of the old round report). The fog-of-war gradient then shows the age of ownership too. News is structured, so it shows in the visuals and the game's tracking ("Information as a structured asset"). Travel comes first in this item. Every traveller, envoys, servants, gold and the news they carry, moves along a route of provinces, with one measure of distance for everything: steps along the province map weighted by terrain, from the map data of items 2 and 5. Journeys therefore differ greatly in length. Interception comes in its simple form. Progress along a route counts in whole-number points that carry over from season to season, so every pace factor matters, even one worth only days ("What sets a company's pace"). Each season the check falls on one province of the stretch the traveller crossed, picked by the share of the season he spent in each, the time on a connection counting in the province whose half of it he is on ("A road belongs to the land it crosses"), so a fast company cannot slip through a bandit province untouched and a slow one is not singled out by where it happens to stop; there a hostile army, an outlaw band or the lawlessness of the place may stop him, with the odds shaped by his skill, his escort, policing and roads, so whether he arrives at all depends on the route he takes. A host can stop anyone passing through his land; a traveller who sneaks through is found only by a chance check weighing his skills and what he carries against the host's policing there ("Passage and access"). At sea, a blockade decides, not walls (decided 20 October 2026, answering item 5's review): troops can land, and a besieged island or coastal city be supplied, only where the enemy's fleets do not hold that province's coastal waters. The seas are redrawn first, with coastal waters per coastal province, a few open-sea crossings, the sailing season and currents as data ("Finer seas", decided 21 October 2026). It is one rule for every island and coast, Alashiya's among them; it replaces whatever item 5 built to protect islands in its place; first guesses, tuned in item 18. Times and odds start from the present pace of letters and what is realistic for the period, and item 18 tunes them ("Distance and travel" and "Interception on the road"). Until item 11b, a report or letter from abroad travels the route by itself, as if the engine carried it; item 11b gives it a real carrier ("Messengers are errands"). Mountain passes are slow and dangerous in winter, by the same season as the sea, and never closed ("Winter is dangerous, never closed"), and travel along a river can take longer upstream than down ("Land and climate" and "Rivers"). Nature stops travellers in the same check as armies and outlaws (river floods join the check when item 10+ builds them), and a traveller chooses his route from what he knows ("Interception on the road" and "Choosing a route"). The land map is reviewed in the same item: distance by length of connection; Aleppo, Qatna, Alalakh, Nuhashshe, Jerusalem, Shechem, Arrapha, Sidon and Arwad added, Kumidi judged by the same bar, and Ṣumur built both ways; places named for their time, Cyprus as east and west; desert and mountain connections; historical routes and attested times; the great rivers drawn as borders where they were frontiers, crossed at fords and ferry towns, and as spines where people lived along them, with river waters for boats ("A border or a spine" under "Rivers"); Nubia; and the edges: Dilmun with a Gulf sea zone, the Kaska lands and the Sutean steppe ("Map review").

   **Built in two parts** (decided 21 October 2026), each its own pull request with its own stop for review, since the item has grown into two items' worth:
   - **7a. The map and the seas.** First, Haakon's answers to item 6c's review (27 October 2026): a threat to a king's capital always paid, from a reserve the budget keeps, and the Counsel preset's narrator on the large model ("Minds follow what is at stake"); and, in a pull request of its own, the pacing design notes (`docs/design/05-pacing-sleeping-seats.md`, over 50 KB) split by topic with nothing else changed (answering item 6b's review). Then the land map review ("Map review"): the added provinces, Kumidi judged by the same bar, names of their time, Cyprus as east and west, Ṣumur built both ways, desert and mountain connections, historical routes and attested times, Nubia, and the edges (Dilmun with a Gulf sea zone, the Kaska lands, the Sutean steppe); and the seas redrawn ("Finer seas"), with coastal waters per coastal province, open-sea crossings, the sailing season and currents, and blockade deciding at sea. **Stop for review:** the map on a phone, the Levant above all.
   - **7b. Travel and news.** First, Haakon's answers to item 7a's review (27 October 2026): Ṣumur a province of its own, with the phone made to read the Levant before anything is given up ("Map on small screens"), checked on a 390-pixel screen; and Lukka a land without a king, like the Kaska lands (since revised: item 11+ gives each one leader, "Land without a ruler"). Then routes and the one measure of distance on the finished map, with one rule for what sets a company's pace, for armies, caravans, couriers and envoys alike, built once as one function whose factors stay neutral until the item that brings their system turns them on ("What sets a company's pace": terrain, river crossings, winter passes, the sea and sneaking are on from here); passes closed in winter and rivers slower upstream; interception in its simple form, with nature in the same check; passage and sneaking through a host's land; choosing a route; news travelling with people, and distant provinces shown in their last known state with its date; reports from abroad travelling by themselves until item 11b. Built after 7a. **Stop for review.**
